results.prompt: Use official Slurm docs to explain QOS limits such as MaxJobs and MaxCPUs
results.agent_response:
Summary
- QOS limits in Slurm control how many jobs and how many resources (CPUs, memory, GPUs, etc.) a QOS, user, account, partition or cluster may consume.
- Limits are configured in the Slurm DB (sacctmgr) and follow a hierarchy (partition QOS → job QOS → user association → account → cluster → partition defaults). See the Slurm docs: resource_limits and qos pages.

Key limit types and what they mean (official-doc semantics)

1) MaxJobs / MaxSubmitJobs
- MaxJobs
  - Limits the number of jobs for the entity (commonly interpreted as the number of concurrently active jobs for that QOS/association). If starting a job would cause the MaxJobs limit to be exceeded, the job will not be considered for allocation (it will pend) unless DenyOnLimit is set (see below). (resource_limits, sacctmgr docs)
- MaxSubmitJobs
  - Controls how many jobs may be submitted/from that entity (submit-time throttling). It’s a separate cap than MaxJobs; both can be present and the effective limits follow the hierarchy rules. (resource_limits)
- Example related fields for aggregates:
  - GrpJobs — maximum number of running jobs in aggregate for that QOS (or association).

2) CPU limits (MaxCPUs and the TRES model)
- Slurm tracks consumable resources as TRES (Trackable RESources). CPU limits are expressed as the cpu TRES (cpu=N).
- Common ways to limit CPU usage via QOS/associations:
  - MaxTRESPerJob=cpu=N — maximum CPUs a single job may request.
  - MaxTRESPerUser=cpu=N — maximum CPUs a single user may have in use (or concurrently allocated), when set on the QOS/association.
  - GrpTRES=cpu=N — group aggregate CPU limit (aggregate across that QOS/account).
- Partition-level and configuration-level CPU caps exist too:
  - Partition/partition-defaults can specify MaxCPUsPerNode, MaxCPUsPerSocket, MaxNodes, etc., which affect how many CPUs can be allocated from nodes. (scontrol / partition docs; cpu_management docs)
- In practice: to limit "MaxCPUs" for a QOS you typically set MaxTRES* entries for cpu (e.g., MaxTRESPerUser=cpu=128 or MaxTRESPerJob=cpu=32), or set GrpTRES for aggregate caps. (sacctmgr / resource_limits docs)

3) Interaction, precedence, and enforcement behavior
- Precedence/hierarchy: limits defined on a Partition QOS or Job QOS will take precedence over association limits (user/account) unless Flags=OverPartQOS is used to reverse precedence. If the same limit is present in multiple places, the first point in the hierarchy is used. (resource_limits)
- Default enforcement behavior:
  - By default, if a job would exceed a limit when considered together with other jobs, the job will pend (not be denied). If you want jobs that individually would violate a “Max” limit to be rejected at submission time, set the QOS flag DenyOnLimit. (qos docs)
- Accounting enforcement:
  - Limit enforcement requires accounting enforcement to be enabled (AccountingStorageEnforce must include limits in slurm.conf). If enforcement is disabled, limits may be recorded but not enforced. (accounting/resource_limits docs)

4) Group/aggregate limits and special cases
- GrpTRES, GrpJobs, GrpSubmitJobs etc. are aggregate/group limits that are checked when attempting to start a job. If starting a job would cause a group limit to be exceeded, that job won’t be considered for scheduling. (sacctmgr docs)
- GRES (generic resources, e.g., GPUs): type-specific limits can be set (e.g., MaxTRESPerUser=gres/gpu:tesla=1) but there is a caveat: if a user requests a generic --gres=gpu:2 (without specifying type), a type-specific limit may not always be enforced (design limitation). The docs recommend using a submit plugin to enforce model-specific behavior when needed. (resource_limits)

How to view / set these (doc-guided commands)
- View QOS limits: sacctmgr show qos format=... (see sacctmgr docs and qos page).
- Set/modify limits: sacctmgr create/modify qos ... or sacctmgr modify assoc ... (sacctmgr manpage and examples in the sacctmgr docs).
- Examples in the docs:
  - sacctmgr modify user where name=<user> set MaxJobs=4 MaxTRESPerUser=cpu=64
  - sacctmgr modify qos name=<qos> set GrpTRES=cpu=200,mem=500G Flags=DenyOnLimit
  (See sacctmgr and qos documentation for precise syntax and available fields.)

Pointers to the official documentation (read first)
- QOS page (limits, DenyOnLimit, OverPartQOS): https://slurm.schedmd.com/qos.html
- Resource Limits (hierarchy, TRES, group limits, examples): https://slurm.schedmd.com/resource_limits.html
- sacctmgr (fields and how to create/modify QOS/associations): https://slurm.schedmd.com/sacctmgr.html
- Job reason codes (you’ll see reason codes when jobs pend due to limits): https://slurm.schedmd.com/job_reason_codes.html

If you want, I can:
- Show the current QOS limits on your cluster (sacctmgr / scontrol) — tell me which QOS or association to inspect and I’ll run the appropriate read command.
- Draft example sacctmgr commands to implement specific MaxJobs/Max-CPU policies you want (include target QOS/account/user and exact numeric limits).

Scheduling policy information must be stored in a database
as specified by the AccountingStorageType configuration parameter
in the slurm.conf configuration file.
Information can be recorded in a [MySQL](http://www.mysql.com/) or

SlurmDBD also uses an existing Slurm accounting storage plugin

SlurmDBD uses data caching and prioritization of pending requests
in order to optimize performance.

and database use, the other Slurm commands and daemons are not required

Job scheduling priority is made up of a number of factors as
described in the [priority/multifactor](https://slurm.schedmd.com/priority_multifactor.html) plugin. One

calculation, the "PriorityWeightQOS" configuration parameter must be
defined in the slurm.conf file and assigned an integer value greater
than zero.

multi-factor plugin is loaded.

## Partition QOS [#partition](https://slurm.schedmd.com/qos.html)
A QOS can be attached to a partition. This means the partition will have all
the same limits as the QOS. This does not associate jobs with the QOS, nor does
it give the job any priority or preemption characteristics of the assigned QOS.
Jobs may separately request the same QOS or a different QOS to gain those
characteristics. However, the Partition QOS limits will override the job's QOS.
If the opposite is desired you may configure the job's QOS with
`Flags=OverPartQOS` which will reverse the order of precedence.
This functionality may be used to implement a true "floating"
partition, in which a partition may access a limited amount of resources with no
restrictions on which nodes it uses to get the resources. This is accomplished

Starting in Slurm 23.11, a QOS may be configured to contain relative resource
limits instead of absolute limits by setting `Flags=Relative`.
When this flag is set, all resource limits are treated as percentages of the
total resources available. Values higher than 100 are interpreted as 100%.

be displayed, the limits will be enforced as a percentage (1MB = 1%).

Slurm's hierarchical limits are enforced in the following order
with Job QOS and Partition QOS order being reversible by using the QOS
flag 'OverPartQOS':
- Partition QOS limit

- Root/Cluster association
- Partition limit
- None

Since the associations in the system follow a hierarchy, so does the
file. Anything that is a parent needs to be defined before any
children. The only exception is the understood 'root' account. This
is always a default for any cluster and does not need to be defined.
To edit/create a file start with a cluster line for the new cluster:
```text
Cluster - cluster_name:MaxTRESPerJob=node=15
```

## Hierarchy[#hierarchy](https://slurm.schedmd.com/resource_limits.html)
Slurm's hierarchical limits are enforced in the following order
with Job QOS and Partition QOS order being reversible by using the QOS
flag 'OverPartQOS':
- Partition QOS limit
- Job QOS limit
- User association
- Account association(s), ascending the hierarchy
- Root/Cluster association
- Partition limit
- None
Note: If limits are defined at multiple points in this hierarchy,
the point in this list where the limit is first defined will be used.
Consider the following example:
- MaxJobs=20 and MaxSubmitJobs is undefined in the partition QOS
- No limits are set in the job QOS and
- MaxJobs=4 and MaxSubmitJobs=50 in the user association
The limits in effect will be MaxJobs=20 and MaxSubmitJobs=50.
Note: The precedence order specified above is respected except for the
following limits: Max[Time|Wall], [Min|Max]Nodes. For these limits, even

### Specific limits over GRES [#gres_limits](https://slurm.schedmd.com/resource_limits.html)
When a GRES has a type associated with it and a limit is applied
over this specific type (e.g. MaxTRESPerUser=gres/gpu:tesla=1 ) if a
user requests a generic gres, the type's limit will not be enforced. In this
situation an additional lua job submit plugin to check the user request may
become useful. For example, if one requests --gres=gpu:2 having a
limit set of MaxTRESPerUser=gres/gpu:tesla=1 , the limit won't be
enforced so it will still be possible to get two teslas.
This is due to a design limitation. The only way to enforce such a limit

In Step 1, Slurm selects the set of nodes from which CPU resources are to be allocated to a job or
job step. Node selection is therefore influenced by many of the configuration and command line options
that control the allocation of CPUs (Step 2 below).

to the job/step. If SelectType is configured to be
select/cons_tres ,
individual sockets, cores and threads may be allocated from the selected nodes as
[consumable resources](https://slurm.schedmd.com/cons_tres.html). The consumable resource type is defined by

When a federated cluster receives a job submission, it will submit copies of the

### Job Scheduling Priority [#priority](https://slurm.schedmd.com/qos.html)
Job scheduling priority is made up of a number of factors as
described in the [priority/multifactor](https://slurm.schedmd.com/priority_multifactor.html) plugin. One
of the factors is the QOS priority. Each QOS is defined in the Slurm
database and includes an associated priority. Jobs that request and
are permitted a QOS will incorporate the priority associated with that
QOS in the job's [multi-factor priority calculation.](https://slurm.schedmd.com/priority_multifactor.html)
To enable the QOS priority component of the multi-factor priority
calculation, the "PriorityWeightQOS" configuration parameter must be
defined in the slurm.conf file and assigned an integer value greater
than zero.
A job's QOS only affects is scheduling priority when the
multi-factor plugin is loaded.

### Job Preemption [#preemption](https://slurm.schedmd.com/qos.html)
Slurm offers two ways for a queued job to preempt a running job,
free-up the running job's resources and allocate them to the queued
job. See the [Preemption description](https://slurm.schedmd.com/preempt.html) for
details.
The preemption method is determined by the "PreemptType"
configuration parameter defined in slurm.conf. When the "PreemptType"
is set to "preempt/qos", a queued job's QOS will be used to determine
whether it can preempt a running job. It is important to note that the QOS
used to determine if a job is eligible for preemption is the QOS associated
with the job and not a [Partition QOS](https://slurm.schedmd.com/qos.html).
The QOS can be assigned (using sacctmgr ) a list of other
QOSs that it can preempt. When there is a queued job with a QOS that
is allowed to preempt a running job of another QOS, the Slurm

## Partition QOS [#partition](https://slurm.schedmd.com/qos.html)
A QOS can be attached to a partition. This means the partition will have all
the same limits as the QOS. This does not associate jobs with the QOS, nor does
it give the job any priority or preemption characteristics of the assigned QOS.
Jobs may separately request the same QOS or a different QOS to gain those
characteristics. However, the Partition QOS limits will override the job's QOS.
If the opposite is desired you may configure the job's QOS with
`Flags=OverPartQOS` which will reverse the order of precedence.
This functionality may be used to implement a true "floating"
partition, in which a partition may access a limited amount of resources with no
restrictions on which nodes it uses to get the resources. This is accomplished
by assigning all nodes to the partition, then configuring a Partition QOS with
`GrpTRES` set to the desired resource limits.

## Backfill Scheduling [#backfill](https://slurm.schedmd.com/sched_config.html)
The backfill scheduling plugin is loaded by default.
Without backfill scheduling, each partition is scheduled strictly in priority
order, which typically results in significantly lower system utilization and
responsiveness than otherwise possible.
Backfill scheduling will start lower priority jobs if doing so does not delay
the expected start time of any higher priority jobs.
Since the expected start time of pending jobs depends upon the expected
completion time of running jobs, reasonably accurate time limits are important
for backfill scheduling to work well.
Slurm's backfill scheduler takes into consideration every running job.

each will start, taking into consideration the possibility of

Summary
- QOS limits in Slurm control how many jobs and how many resources (CPUs, memory, GPUs, etc.) a QOS, user, account, partition or cluster may consume.
- Limits are configured in the Slurm DB (sacctmgr) and follow a hierarchy (partition QOS → job QOS → user association → account → cluster → partition defaults). See the Slurm docs: resource_limits and qos pages.

Key limit types and what they mean (official-doc semantics)

1) MaxJobs / MaxSubmitJobs
- MaxJobs
  - Limits the number of jobs for the entity (commonly interpreted as the number of concurrently active jobs for that QOS/association). If starting a job would cause the MaxJobs limit to be exceeded, the job will not be considered for allocation (it will pend) unless DenyOnLimit is set (see below). (resource_limits, sacctmgr docs)
- MaxSubmitJobs
  - Controls how many jobs may be submitted/from that entity (submit-time throttling). It’s a separate cap than MaxJobs; both can be present and the effective limits follow the hierarchy rules. (resource_limits)
- Example related fields for aggregates:
  - GrpJobs — maximum number of running jobs in aggregate for that QOS (or association).

2) CPU limits (MaxCPUs and the TRES model)
- Slurm tracks consumable resources as TRES (Trackable RESources). CPU limits are expressed as the cpu TRES (cpu=N).
- Common ways to limit CPU usage via QOS/associations:
  - MaxTRESPerJob=cpu=N — maximum CPUs a single job may request.
  - MaxTRESPerUser=cpu=N — maximum CPUs a single user may have in use (or concurrently allocated), when set on the QOS/association.
  - GrpTRES=cpu=N — group aggregate CPU limit (aggregate across that QOS/account).
- Partition-level and configuration-level CPU caps exist too:
  - Partition/partition-defaults can specify MaxCPUsPerNode, MaxCPUsPerSocket, MaxNodes, etc., which affect how many CPUs can be allocated from nodes. (scontrol / partition docs; cpu_management docs)
- In practice: to limit "MaxCPUs" for a QOS you typically set MaxTRES* entries for cpu (e.g., MaxTRESPerUser=cpu=128 or MaxTRESPerJob=cpu=32), or set GrpTRES for aggregate caps. (sacctmgr / resource_limits docs)

3) Interaction, precedence, and enforcement behavior
- Precedence/hierarchy: limits defined on a Partition QOS or Job QOS will take precedence over association limits (user/account) unless Flags=OverPartQOS is used to reverse precedence. If the same limit is present in multiple places, the first point in the hierarchy is used. (resource_limits)
- Default enforcement behavior:
  - By default, if a job would exceed a limit when considered together with other jobs, the job will pend (not be denied). If you want jobs that individually would violate a “Max” limit to be rejected at submission time, set the QOS flag DenyOnLimit. (qos docs)
- Accounting enforcement:
  - Limit enforcement requires accounting enforcement to be enabled (AccountingStorageEnforce must include limits in slurm.conf). If enforcement is disabled, limits may be recorded but not enforced. (accounting/resource_limits docs)

4) Group/aggregate limits and special cases
- GrpTRES, GrpJobs, GrpSubmitJobs etc. are aggregate/group limits that are checked when attempting to start a job. If starting a job would cause a group limit to be exceeded, that job won’t be considered for scheduling. (sacctmgr docs)
- GRES (generic resources, e.g., GPUs): type-specific limits can be set (e.g., MaxTRESPerUser=gres/gpu:tesla=1) but there is a caveat: if a user requests a generic --gres=gpu:2 (without specifying type), a type-specific limit may not always be enforced (design limitation). The docs recommend using a submit plugin to enforce model-specific behavior when needed. (resource_limits)

How to view / set these (doc-guided commands)
- View QOS limits: sacctmgr show qos format=... (see sacctmgr docs and qos page).
- Set/modify limits: sacctmgr create/modify qos ... or sacctmgr modify assoc ... (sacctmgr manpage and examples in the sacctmgr docs).
- Examples in the docs:
  - sacctmgr modify user where name=<user> set MaxJobs=4 MaxTRESPerUser=cpu=64
  - sacctmgr modify qos name=<qos> set GrpTRES=cpu=200,mem=500G Flags=DenyOnLimit
  (See sacctmgr and qos documentation for precise syntax and available fields.)

Pointers to the official documentation (read first)
- QOS page (limits, DenyOnLimit, OverPartQOS): https://slurm.schedmd.com/qos.html
- Resource Limits (hierarchy, TRES, group limits, examples): https://slurm.schedmd.com/resource_limits.html
- sacctmgr (fields and how to create/modify QOS/associations): https://slurm.schedmd.com/sacctmgr.html
- Job reason codes (you’ll see reason codes when jobs pend due to limits): https://slurm.schedmd.com/job_reason_codes.html

If you want, I can:
- Show the current QOS limits on your cluster (sacctmgr / scontrol) — tell me which QOS or association to inspect and I’ll run the appropriate read command.
- Draft example sacctmgr commands to implement specific MaxJobs/Max-CPU policies you want (include target QOS/account/user and exact numeric limits).

## Hierarchy[#hierarchy](https://slurm.schedmd.com/resource_limits.html)
Slurm's hierarchical limits are enforced in the following order
with Job QOS and Partition QOS order being reversible by using the QOS
flag 'OverPartQOS':
- Partition QOS limit
- Job QOS limit
- User association
- Account association(s), ascending the hierarchy
- Root/Cluster association
- Partition limit
- None
Note: If limits are defined at multiple points in this hierarchy,

## Partition QOS [#partition](https://slurm.schedmd.com/qos.html)
A QOS can be attached to a partition. This means the partition will have all
the same limits as the QOS. This does not associate jobs with the QOS, nor does
it give the job any priority or preemption characteristics of the assigned QOS.
Jobs may separately request the same QOS or a different QOS to gain those
characteristics. However, the Partition QOS limits will override the job's QOS.
If the opposite is desired you may configure the job's QOS with
`Flags=OverPartQOS` which will reverse the order of precedence.
This functionality may be used to implement a true "floating"
partition, in which a partition may access a limited amount of resources with no
restrictions on which nodes it uses to get the resources. This is accomplished
by assigning all nodes to the partition, then configuring a Partition QOS with
`GrpTRES` set to the desired resource limits.

Starting in Slurm 23.11, a QOS may be configured to contain relative resource
limits instead of absolute limits by setting `Flags=Relative`.
When this flag is set, all resource limits are treated as percentages of the
total resources available. Values higher than 100 are interpreted as 100%.

be displayed, the limits will be enforced as a percentage (1MB = 1%).

## Configuration[#config](https://slurm.schedmd.com/resource_limits.html)
Scheduling policy information must be stored in a database
as specified by the AccountingStorageType configuration parameter
in the slurm.conf configuration file.
Information can be recorded in a [MySQL](http://www.mysql.com/) or
[MariaDB](https://mariadb.org/) database.
For security and performance reasons, the use of
SlurmDBD (Slurm Database Daemon) as a front-end to the
database is strongly recommended.
SlurmDBD uses a Slurm authentication plugin (e.g. MUNGE).
SlurmDBD also uses an existing Slurm accounting storage plugin
to maximize code reuse.
SlurmDBD uses data caching and prioritization of pending requests
in order to optimize performance.
While SlurmDBD relies upon existing Slurm plugins for authentication
and database use, the other Slurm commands and daemons are not required
on the host where SlurmDBD is installed.

Trackable RESources (TRES) are used in many QOS or Association limits
(GrpTRES* / MaxTRES*). When setting limits, one or more comma-separated

Each TRES can be one of the Slurm defaults (e.g., cpu , mem ,
node ), or any defined generic resource. You can see the list of available
resources by running sacctmgr show tres .

establish 2 different limits: one for 16 CPUs and another for 32 GB of memory.

subsequent assignment of "GrpTRES=gres/gpu=2" will result in

## Hierarchy[#hierarchy](https://slurm.schedmd.com/resource_limits.html)
Slurm's hierarchical limits are enforced in the following order
with Job QOS and Partition QOS order being reversible by using the QOS
flag 'OverPartQOS':
- Partition QOS limit
- Job QOS limit
- User association
- Account association(s), ascending the hierarchy
- Root/Cluster association
- Partition limit
- None
Note: If limits are defined at multiple points in this hierarchy,
the point in this list where the limit is first defined will be used.
Consider the following example:
- MaxJobs=20 and MaxSubmitJobs is undefined in the partition QOS
- No limits are set in the job QOS and
- MaxJobs=4 and MaxSubmitJobs=50 in the user association
The limits in effect will be MaxJobs=20 and MaxSubmitJobs=50.

following limits: Max[Time|Wall], [Min|Max]Nodes. For these limits, even

[consumable resources](https://slurm.schedmd.com/cons_tres.html). The consumable resource type is defined by

When a federated cluster receives a job submission, it will submit copies of the
job ( sibling jobs ) to each eligible cluster. Each cluster will then
independently attempt to schedule the job.

Slurm's hierarchical limits are enforced in the following order
with Job QOS and Partition QOS order being reversible by using the QOS
flag 'OverPartQOS':
- Partition QOS limit
- Job QOS limit
- User association
- Account association(s), ascending the hierarchy
- Root/Cluster association
- Partition limit
- None
Note: If limits are defined at multiple points in this hierarchy,
the point in this list where the limit is first defined will be used.

### Job Scheduling Priority [#priority](https://slurm.schedmd.com/qos.html)
Job scheduling priority is made up of a number of factors as
described in the [priority/multifactor](https://slurm.schedmd.com/priority_multifactor.html) plugin. One
of the factors is the QOS priority. Each QOS is defined in the Slurm
database and includes an associated priority. Jobs that request and
are permitted a QOS will incorporate the priority associated with that
QOS in the job's [multi-factor priority calculation.](https://slurm.schedmd.com/priority_multifactor.html)
To enable the QOS priority component of the multi-factor priority
calculation, the "PriorityWeightQOS" configuration parameter must be

The backfill scheduling plugin is loaded by default.
Without backfill scheduling, each partition is scheduled strictly in priority
order, which typically results in significantly lower system utilization and
responsiveness than otherwise possible.

the expected start time of any higher priority jobs.

Based on the current cluster state, summary
- QOS limits in Slurm control how many jobs and how many resources (CPUs, memory, GPUs, etc.) a QOS, user, account, partition or cluster may consume.
- Limits are configured in the Slurm DB (sacctmgr) and follow a hierarchy (partition QOS → job QOS → user association → account → cluster → partition defaults). See the Slurm docs: resource_limits and qos pages.

Key limit types and what they mean (official-doc semantics)

1) MaxJobs / MaxSubmitJobs
- MaxJobs
  - Limits the number of jobs for the entity (commonly interpreted as the number of concurrently active jobs for that QOS/association). If starting a job would cause the MaxJobs limit to be exceeded, the job will not be considered for allocation (it will pend) unless DenyOnLimit is set (see below). (resource_limits, sacctmgr docs)
- MaxSubmitJobs
  - Controls how many jobs may be submitted/from that entity (submit-time throttling). It’s a separate cap than MaxJobs; both can be present and the effective limits follow the hierarchy rules. (resource_limits)
- Example related fields for aggregates:
  - GrpJobs — maximum number of running jobs in aggregate for that QOS (or association).

2) CPU limits (MaxCPUs and the TRES model)
- Slurm tracks consumable resources as TRES (Trackable RESources). CPU limits are expressed as the cpu TRES (cpu=N).
- Common ways to limit CPU usage via QOS/associations:
  - MaxTRESPerJob=cpu=N — maximum CPUs a single job may request.
  - MaxTRESPerUser=cpu=N — maximum CPUs a single user may have in use (or concurrently allocated), when set on the QOS/association.
  - GrpTRES=cpu=N — group aggregate CPU limit (aggregate across that QOS/account).
- Partition-level and configuration-level CPU caps exist too:
  - Partition/partition-defaults can specify MaxCPUsPerNode, MaxCPUsPerSocket, MaxNodes, etc., which affect how many CPUs can be allocated from nodes. (scontrol / partition docs; cpu_management docs)
- In practice: to limit "MaxCPUs" for a QOS you typically set MaxTRES* entries for cpu (e.g., MaxTRESPerUser=cpu=128 or MaxTRESPerJob=cpu=32), or set GrpTRES for aggregate caps. (sacctmgr / resource_limits docs)

3) Interaction, precedence, and enforcement behavior
- Precedence/hierarchy: limits defined on a Partition QOS or Job QOS will take precedence over association limits (user/account) unless Flags=OverPartQOS is used to reverse precedence. If the same limit is present in multiple places, the first point in the hierarchy is used. (resource_limits)
- Default enforcement behavior:
  - By default, if a job would exceed a limit when considered together with other jobs, the job will pend (not be denied). If you want jobs that individually would violate a “Max” limit to be rejected at submission time, set the QOS flag DenyOnLimit. (qos docs)
- Accounting enforcement:
  - Limit enforcement requires accounting enforcement to be enabled (AccountingStorageEnforce must include limits in slurm.conf). If enforcement is disabled, limits may be recorded but not enforced. (accounting/resource_limits docs)

4) Group/aggregate limits and special cases
- GrpTRES, GrpJobs, GrpSubmitJobs etc. are aggregate/group limits that are checked when attempting to start a job. If starting a job would cause a group limit to be exceeded, that job won’t be considered for scheduling. (sacctmgr docs)
- GRES (generic resources, e.g., GPUs): type-specific limits can be set (e.g., MaxTRESPerUser=gres/gpu:tesla=1) but there is a caveat: if a user requests a generic --gres=gpu:2 (without specifying type), a type-specific limit may not always be enforced (design limitation). The docs recommend using a submit plugin to enforce model-specific behavior when needed. (resource_limits)

How to view / set these (doc-guided commands)
- View QOS limits: sacctmgr show qos format=... (see sacctmgr docs and qos page).
- Set/modify limits: sacctmgr create/modify qos ... or sacctmgr modify assoc ... (sacctmgr manpage and examples in the sacctmgr docs).
- Examples in the docs:
  - sacctmgr modify user where name=<user> set MaxJobs=4 MaxTRESPerUser=cpu=64
  - sacctmgr modify qos name=<qos> set GrpTRES=cpu=200,mem=500G Flags=DenyOnLimit
  (See sacctmgr and qos documentation for precise syntax and available fields.)

Pointers to the official documentation (read first)
- QOS page (limits, DenyOnLimit, OverPartQOS): https://slurm.schedmd.com/qos.html
- Resource Limits (hierarchy, TRES, group limits, examples): https://slurm.schedmd.com/resource_limits.html
- sacctmgr (fields and how to create/modify QOS/associations): https://slurm.schedmd.com/sacctmgr.html
- Job reason codes (you’ll see reason codes when jobs pend due to limits): https://slurm.schedmd.com/job_reason_codes.html

Slurm's hierarchical limits are enforced in the following order
with Job QOS and Partition QOS order being reversible by using the QOS
flag 'OverPartQOS':
- Partition QOS limit
- Job QOS limit
- User association
- Account association(s), ascending the hierarchy
- Root/Cluster association
- Partition limit
- None

the point in this list where the limit is first defined will be used.

Scheduling policy information must be stored in a database
as specified by the AccountingStorageType configuration parameter
in the slurm.conf configuration file.
Information can be recorded in a [MySQL](http://www.mysql.com/) or
[MariaDB](https://mariadb.org/) database.
For security and performance reasons, the use of
SlurmDBD (Slurm Database Daemon) as a front-end to the
database is strongly recommended.

SlurmDBD also uses an existing Slurm accounting storage plugin
to maximize code reuse.
SlurmDBD uses data caching and prioritization of pending requests
in order to optimize performance.

and database use, the other Slurm commands and daemons are not required
on the host where SlurmDBD is installed.

Job scheduling priority is made up of a number of factors as
described in the [priority/multifactor](https://slurm.schedmd.com/priority_multifactor.html) plugin. One

calculation, the "PriorityWeightQOS" configuration parameter must be
defined in the slurm.conf file and assigned an integer value greater
than zero.

multi-factor plugin is loaded.

## Configuration[#config](https://slurm.schedmd.com/resource_limits.html)
Scheduling policy information must be stored in a database
as specified by the AccountingStorageType configuration parameter
in the slurm.conf configuration file.
Information can be recorded in a [MySQL](http://www.mysql.com/) or
[MariaDB](https://mariadb.org/) database.
For security and performance reasons, the use of
SlurmDBD (Slurm Database Daemon) as a front-end to the
database is strongly recommended.
SlurmDBD uses a Slurm authentication plugin (e.g. MUNGE).
SlurmDBD also uses an existing Slurm accounting storage plugin
to maximize code reuse.
SlurmDBD uses data caching and prioritization of pending requests
in order to optimize performance.

## Job Submission [#jobsubmission](https://slurm.schedmd.com/federation.html)
When a federated cluster receives a job submission, it will submit copies of the
job ( sibling jobs ) to each eligible cluster. Each cluster will then
independently attempt to schedule the job.
Jobs can be directed to specific clusters in the federation using the
-M,--clusters=<cluster_list> and the new
--cluster-constraint=[!]<constraint_list> options.
Using the -M,--clusters=<cluster_list> the submission command
(sbatch, salloc, srun) will pick one cluster from the list of clusters to submit
the job to and will also pass along the list of clusters with the job. The
clusters in the list will be the only viable clusters that siblings jobs can be

## Hierarchy[#hierarchy](https://slurm.schedmd.com/resource_limits.html)
Slurm's hierarchical limits are enforced in the following order
with Job QOS and Partition QOS order being reversible by using the QOS
flag 'OverPartQOS':
- Partition QOS limit
- Job QOS limit
- User association
- Account association(s), ascending the hierarchy
- Root/Cluster association
- Partition limit
- None
Note: If limits are defined at multiple points in this hierarchy,
the point in this list where the limit is first defined will be used.
Consider the following example:
- MaxJobs=20 and MaxSubmitJobs is undefined in the partition QOS
- No limits are set in the job QOS and
- MaxJobs=4 and MaxSubmitJobs=50 in the user association
The limits in effect will be MaxJobs=20 and MaxSubmitJobs=50.
Note: The precedence order specified above is respected except for the
following limits: Max[Time|Wall], [Min|Max]Nodes. For these limits, even

Slurm's hierarchical limits are enforced in the following order

flag 'OverPartQOS':
- Partition QOS limit
- Job QOS limit

- None

Job scheduling priority is made up of a number of factors as
described in the [priority/multifactor](https://slurm.schedmd.com/priority_multifactor.html) plugin. One

Slurm offers two ways for a queued job to preempt a running job,

A QOS can be attached to a partition. This means the partition will have all
the same limits as the QOS. This does not associate jobs with the QOS, nor does
it give the job any priority or preemption characteristics of the assigned QOS.

The backfill scheduling plugin is loaded by default.
Without backfill scheduling, each partition is scheduled strictly in priority
order, which typically results in significantly lower system utilization and
responsiveness than otherwise possible.

- QOS limits in Slurm control how many jobs and how many resources (CPUs, memory, GPUs, etc.) a QOS, user, account, partition or cluster may consume.
- Limits are configured in the Slurm DB (sacctmgr) and follow a hierarchy (partition QOS → job QOS → user association → account → cluster → partition defaults). See the Slurm docs: resource_limits and qos pages.

Key limit types and what they mean (official-doc semantics)

1) MaxJobs / MaxSubmitJobs
- MaxJobs
  - Limits the number of jobs for the entity (commonly interpreted as the number of concurrently active jobs for that QOS/association). If starting a job would cause the MaxJobs limit to be exceeded, the job will not be considered for allocation (it will pend) unless DenyOnLimit is set (see below). (resource_limits, sacctmgr docs)
- MaxSubmitJobs
  - Controls how many jobs may be submitted/from that entity (submit-time throttling). It’s a separate cap than MaxJobs; both can be present and the effective limits follow the hierarchy rules. (resource_limits)
- Example related fields for aggregates:
  - GrpJobs — maximum number of running jobs in aggregate for that QOS (or association).

2) CPU limits (MaxCPUs and the TRES model)
- Slurm tracks consumable resources as TRES (Trackable RESources). CPU limits are expressed as the cpu TRES (cpu=N).
- Common ways to limit CPU usage via QOS/associations:
  - MaxTRESPerJob=cpu=N — maximum CPUs a single job may request.
  - MaxTRESPerUser=cpu=N — maximum CPUs a single user may have in use (or concurrently allocated), when set on the QOS/association.
  - GrpTRES=cpu=N — group aggregate CPU limit (aggregate across that QOS/account).
- Partition-level and configuration-level CPU caps exist too:
  - Partition/partition-defaults can specify MaxCPUsPerNode, MaxCPUsPerSocket, MaxNodes, etc., which affect how many CPUs can be allocated from nodes. (scontrol / partition docs; cpu_management docs)
- In practice: to limit "MaxCPUs" for a QOS you typically set MaxTRES* entries for cpu (e.g., MaxTRESPerUser=cpu=128 or MaxTRESPerJob=cpu=32), or set GrpTRES for aggregate caps. (sacctmgr / resource_limits docs)

3) Interaction, precedence, and enforcement behavior
- Precedence/hierarchy: limits defined on a Partition QOS or Job QOS will take precedence over association limits (user/account) unless Flags=OverPartQOS is used to reverse precedence. If the same limit is present in multiple places, the first point in the hierarchy is used. (resource_limits)
- Default enforcement behavior:
  - By default, if a job would exceed a limit when considered together with other jobs, the job will pend (not be denied). If you want jobs that individually would violate a “Max” limit to be rejected at submission time, set the QOS flag DenyOnLimit. (qos docs)
- Accounting enforcement:
  - Limit enforcement requires accounting enforcement to be enabled (AccountingStorageEnforce must include limits in slurm.conf). If enforcement is disabled, limits may be recorded but not enforced. (accounting/resource_limits docs)

4) Group/aggregate limits and special cases
- GrpTRES, GrpJobs, GrpSubmitJobs etc. are aggregate/group limits that are checked when attempting to start a job. If starting a job would cause a group limit to be exceeded, that job won’t be considered for scheduling. (sacctmgr docs)
- GRES (generic resources, e.g., GPUs): type-specific limits can be set (e.g., MaxTRESPerUser=gres/gpu:tesla=1) but there is a caveat: if a user requests a generic --gres=gpu:2 (without specifying type), a type-specific limit may not always be enforced (design limitation). The docs recommend using a submit plugin to enforce model-specific behavior when needed. (resource_limits)

How to view / set these (doc-guided commands)
- View QOS limits: sacctmgr show qos format=... (see sacctmgr docs and qos page).
- Set/modify limits: sacctmgr create/modify qos ... or sacctmgr modify assoc ... (sacctmgr manpage and examples in the sacctmgr docs).
- Examples in the docs:
  - sacctmgr modify user where name=<user> set MaxJobs=4 MaxTRESPerUser=cpu=64
  - sacctmgr modify qos name=<qos> set GrpTRES=cpu=200,mem=500G Flags=DenyOnLimit
  (See sacctmgr and qos documentation for precise syntax and available fields.)

Starting in Slurm 23.11, a QOS may be configured to contain relative resource
limits instead of absolute limits by setting `Flags=Relative`.
When this flag is set, all resource limits are treated as percentages of the
total resources available. Values higher than 100 are interpreted as 100%.

be displayed, the limits will be enforced as a percentage (1MB = 1%).

resources in the whole cluster. For example, `cpu=50` would be

## Hierarchy[#hierarchy](https://slurm.schedmd.com/resource_limits.html)
Slurm's hierarchical limits are enforced in the following order
with Job QOS and Partition QOS order being reversible by using the QOS
flag 'OverPartQOS':
- Partition QOS limit
- Job QOS limit
- User association
- Account association(s), ascending the hierarchy
- Root/Cluster association
- Partition limit
- None

- MaxJobs=20 and MaxSubmitJobs is undefined in the partition QOS

- MaxJobs=4 and MaxSubmitJobs=50 in the user association

## Configuration[#config](https://slurm.schedmd.com/resource_limits.html)
Scheduling policy information must be stored in a database
as specified by the AccountingStorageType configuration parameter
in the slurm.conf configuration file.
Information can be recorded in a [MySQL](http://www.mysql.com/) or
[MariaDB](https://mariadb.org/) database.
For security and performance reasons, the use of
SlurmDBD (Slurm Database Daemon) as a front-end to the
database is strongly recommended.
SlurmDBD uses a Slurm authentication plugin (e.g. MUNGE).
SlurmDBD also uses an existing Slurm accounting storage plugin
to maximize code reuse.
SlurmDBD uses data caching and prioritization of pending requests
in order to optimize performance.
While SlurmDBD relies upon existing Slurm plugins for authentication
and database use, the other Slurm commands and daemons are not required
on the host where SlurmDBD is installed.

## Tools[#tools](https://slurm.schedmd.com/resource_limits.html)
The tool used to manage accounting policy is sacctmgr .
It can be used to create and delete cluster, user, account,
and partition records plus their combined association record.
See man sacctmgr for details on this tools and examples of
its use.
Changes made to the scheduling policy are uploaded to
the Slurm control daemons on the various clusters and take effect
immediately. When an association is deleted, all running or pending
jobs which belong to that association are immediately canceled.
When limits are lowered, running jobs will not be canceled to
satisfy the new limits, but the new lower limits will be enforced.

### Job Scheduling Priority [#priority](https://slurm.schedmd.com/qos.html)
Job scheduling priority is made up of a number of factors as
described in the [priority/multifactor](https://slurm.schedmd.com/priority_multifactor.html) plugin. One
of the factors is the QOS priority. Each QOS is defined in the Slurm
database and includes an associated priority. Jobs that request and
are permitted a QOS will incorporate the priority associated with that
QOS in the job's [multi-factor priority calculation.](https://slurm.schedmd.com/priority_multifactor.html)
To enable the QOS priority component of the multi-factor priority
calculation, the "PriorityWeightQOS" configuration parameter must be
defined in the slurm.conf file and assigned an integer value greater
than zero.
A job's QOS only affects is scheduling priority when the
multi-factor plugin is loaded.

Slurm offers two ways for a queued job to preempt a running job,
free-up the running job's resources and allocate them to the queued

configuration parameter defined in slurm.conf. When the "PreemptType"
is set to "preempt/qos", a queued job's QOS will be used to determine

QOSs that it can preempt. When there is a queued job with a QOS that

## Relative QOS [#relative](https://slurm.schedmd.com/qos.html)
Starting in Slurm 23.11, a QOS may be configured to contain relative resource
limits instead of absolute limits by setting `Flags=Relative`.
When this flag is set, all resource limits are treated as percentages of the
total resources available. Values higher than 100 are interpreted as 100%.
Memory limits should be set with no units. Although the default units (MB) will
be displayed, the limits will be enforced as a percentage (1MB = 1%).

resources in the whole cluster. For example, `cpu=50` would be

## Hierarchy[#hierarchy](https://slurm.schedmd.com/resource_limits.html)
Slurm's hierarchical limits are enforced in the following order
with Job QOS and Partition QOS order being reversible by using the QOS
flag 'OverPartQOS':
- Partition QOS limit
- Job QOS limit
- User association
- Account association(s), ascending the hierarchy
- Root/Cluster association
- Partition limit
- None
Note: If limits are defined at multiple points in this hierarchy,
the point in this list where the limit is first defined will be used.
Consider the following example:
- MaxJobs=20 and MaxSubmitJobs is undefined in the partition QOS
- No limits are set in the job QOS and
- MaxJobs=4 and MaxSubmitJobs=50 in the user association

## Configuration[#config](https://slurm.schedmd.com/resource_limits.html)
Scheduling policy information must be stored in a database
as specified by the AccountingStorageType configuration parameter
in the slurm.conf configuration file.
Information can be recorded in a [MySQL](http://www.mysql.com/) or
[MariaDB](https://mariadb.org/) database.
For security and performance reasons, the use of
SlurmDBD (Slurm Database Daemon) as a front-end to the
database is strongly recommended.
SlurmDBD uses a Slurm authentication plugin (e.g. MUNGE).
SlurmDBD also uses an existing Slurm accounting storage plugin
to maximize code reuse.
SlurmDBD uses data caching and prioritization of pending requests
in order to optimize performance.

and database use, the other Slurm commands and daemons are not required

## Job Submission [#jobsubmission](https://slurm.schedmd.com/federation.html)
When a federated cluster receives a job submission, it will submit copies of the
job ( sibling jobs ) to each eligible cluster. Each cluster will then
independently attempt to schedule the job.
Jobs can be directed to specific clusters in the federation using the
-M,--clusters=<cluster_list> and the new
--cluster-constraint=[!]<constraint_list> options.
Using the -M,--clusters=<cluster_list> the submission command
(sbatch, salloc, srun) will pick one cluster from the list of clusters to submit
the job to and will also pass along the list of clusters with the job. The
clusters in the list will be the only viable clusters that siblings jobs can be
submitted to. For example the submission:

## Hierarchy[#hierarchy](https://slurm.schedmd.com/resource_limits.html)
Slurm's hierarchical limits are enforced in the following order
with Job QOS and Partition QOS order being reversible by using the QOS
flag 'OverPartQOS':
- Partition QOS limit
- Job QOS limit
- User association
- Account association(s), ascending the hierarchy
- Root/Cluster association
- Partition limit
- None
Note: If limits are defined at multiple points in this hierarchy,
the point in this list where the limit is first defined will be used.
Consider the following example:
- MaxJobs=20 and MaxSubmitJobs is undefined in the partition QOS
- No limits are set in the job QOS and
- MaxJobs=4 and MaxSubmitJobs=50 in the user association

### Job Scheduling Priority [#priority](https://slurm.schedmd.com/qos.html)
Job scheduling priority is made up of a number of factors as
described in the [priority/multifactor](https://slurm.schedmd.com/priority_multifactor.html) plugin. One
of the factors is the QOS priority. Each QOS is defined in the Slurm
database and includes an associated priority. Jobs that request and
are permitted a QOS will incorporate the priority associated with that
QOS in the job's [multi-factor priority calculation.](https://slurm.schedmd.com/priority_multifactor.html)
To enable the QOS priority component of the multi-factor priority
calculation, the "PriorityWeightQOS" configuration parameter must be
defined in the slurm.conf file and assigned an integer value greater
than zero.
A job's QOS only affects is scheduling priority when the
multi-factor plugin is loaded.

### Job Preemption [#preemption](https://slurm.schedmd.com/qos.html)
Slurm offers two ways for a queued job to preempt a running job,
free-up the running job's resources and allocate them to the queued
job. See the [Preemption description](https://slurm.schedmd.com/preempt.html) for
details.
The preemption method is determined by the "PreemptType"
configuration parameter defined in slurm.conf. When the "PreemptType"
is set to "preempt/qos", a queued job's QOS will be used to determine
whether it can preempt a running job. It is important to note that the QOS
used to determine if a job is eligible for preemption is the QOS associated
with the job and not a [Partition QOS](https://slurm.schedmd.com/qos.html).
The QOS can be assigned (using sacctmgr ) a list of other
QOSs that it can preempt. When there is a queued job with a QOS that
is allowed to preempt a running job of another QOS, the Slurm
scheduler will preempt the running job.

## Partition QOS [#partition](https://slurm.schedmd.com/qos.html)
A QOS can be attached to a partition. This means the partition will have all
the same limits as the QOS. This does not associate jobs with the QOS, nor does
it give the job any priority or preemption characteristics of the assigned QOS.
Jobs may separately request the same QOS or a different QOS to gain those
characteristics. However, the Partition QOS limits will override the job's QOS.
If the opposite is desired you may configure the job's QOS with
`Flags=OverPartQOS` which will reverse the order of precedence.
This functionality may be used to implement a true "floating"
partition, in which a partition may access a limited amount of resources with no
restrictions on which nodes it uses to get the resources. This is accomplished
by assigning all nodes to the partition, then configuring a Partition QOS with
`GrpTRES` set to the desired resource limits.

The job submit plugin is invoked independently for each component of a
heterogeneous job.
The spank_init_post_opt() function is invoked once for each component of a

## Limitations [#limitations](https://slurm.schedmd.com/heterogeneous_jobs.html)
The backfill scheduler has limitations in how it tracks usage of CPUs and
memory in the future.
This typically requires the backfill scheduler be able to allocate each
component of a heterogeneous job on a different node in order to begin its
resource allocation, even if multiple components of the job do actually get
allocated resources on the same node.

the cluster from which the job is submitted. The heterogeneous job will not
be eligible to migrate between clusters or to have different components of

## Environment Variables [#env_var](https://slurm.schedmd.com/heterogeneous_jobs.html)
Slurm environment variables will be set independently for each component of
the job by appending "_HET_GROUP_" and a sequence number to the usual name.

## Backfill Scheduling [#backfill](https://slurm.schedmd.com/sched_config.html)
The backfill scheduling plugin is loaded by default.
Without backfill scheduling, each partition is scheduled strictly in priority
order, which typically results in significantly lower system utilization and
responsiveness than otherwise possible.
Backfill scheduling will start lower priority jobs if doing so does not delay
the expected start time of any higher priority jobs.
Since the expected start time of pending jobs depends upon the expected
completion time of running jobs, reasonably accurate time limits are important
for backfill scheduling to work well.
Slurm's backfill scheduler takes into consideration every running job.
It then considers pending jobs in priority order, determining when and where
each will start, taking into consideration the possibility of
[job preemption](https://slurm.schedmd.com/preempt.html),

With this option, all jobs, including both running and queued, and all
node states, will be deleted. Without this option, previously running

## Managing Jobs[#managing](https://slurm.schedmd.com/heterogeneous_jobs.html)
Information maintained in Slurm for a heterogeneous job includes:
- job_id : Each component of a heterogeneous job will have its own unique job_id .
- het_job_id : This identification number applies to all components of the heterogeneous job. All components of the same job will have the same het_job_id value and it will be equal to the job_id of the first component. We refer to this as the "heterogeneous job leader".
- het_job_id_set : Regular expression identifying all job_id values associated with the job.
- het_job_offset : A unique sequence number applied to each component of the heterogeneous job. The first component will have a het_job_offset value of 0, the next a value of 1, etc.

results.prompt: Use official Slurm docs to explain the pending reason Priority
results.agent_response:
Short answer (from the official Slurm docs)

- "Priority" is a job pending reason that means the scheduler attempted to place the job but found one or more jobs with higher scheduling priority for the same partition/nodes. The scheduler therefore left this job pending because other jobs outrank it in the priority ordering. (See Job Reason Codes: "Priority".)

What Slurm uses to compute that priority (from the Multifactor Priority plugin)
- By default Slurm uses the multifactor priority plugin. A job's priority is a weighted sum of enabled factors, for example:
  site_factor + PriorityWeightAge * age_factor + PriorityWeightAssoc * assoc_factor + PriorityWeightFairshare * fairshare_factor + PriorityWeightJobSize * job_size_factor + PriorityWeightPartition * partition_factor + PriorityWeightQOS * QOS_factor + SUM(TRES_weights * TRES_factors) - nice_factor
- Each factor is normalized (0.0–1.0) and the final job priority is an integer (0 .. 4294967295). Higher numbers = higher scheduling precedence. (See priority_multifactor.)

Why you see "Priority" instead of some other reason
- The scheduler reports the first reason it encounters for why the job cannot start. If the scheduling attempt finds higher-priority jobs blocking allocation, it reports "Priority" even if other constraints also apply. (See Job Reason Codes.)

How to inspect and influence this
- Inspect actual per-job priority values and factors with the sprio utility (and sprio --weights to see configured weights).
- Check slurm.conf for PriorityType and the PriorityWeight* settings to see which factors and weights are active.
- Common ways to raise a job's priority: let the job age (age factor), change its QOS or association priority, change nice value, request a partition with higher partition_factor, or adjust fairshare/association/QOS limits (requires admin/config changes).

References (official Slurm docs)
- Job Reason Codes — "Priority" entry: https://slurm.schedmd.com/job_reason_codes.html
- Multifactor Priority plugin (priority factors and formula): https://slurm.schedmd.com/priority_multifactor.html
- sprio / priority tools documentation is linked from the priority page.

If you want, I can show you current priority values for jobs in the queue (sprio) or explain how a specific job's priority is being computed — tell me which job ID to inspect.

## Job Priority Factors In General [#general](https://slurm.schedmd.com/priority_multifactor.html)
The job's priority at any given time will be a weighted sum of all the
factors that have been enabled in the slurm.conf file. Job priority can be
expressed as:
```text
Job_priority = site_factor + (PriorityWeightAge) * (age_factor) + (PriorityWeightAssoc) * (assoc_factor) + (PriorityWeightFairshare) * (fair-share_factor) + (PriorityWeightJobSize) * (job_size_factor) + (PriorityWeightPartition) * (priority_job_factor) + (PriorityWeightQOS) * (QOS_factor) + SUM(TRES_weight_cpu * TRES_factor_cpu, TRES_weight_ * TRES_factor_ , ...) - nice_factor
```
All of the factors in this formula are floating point numbers that
range from 0.0 to 1.0. The weights are unsigned, 32 bit integers.

Snippet:
## PERFORMANCE[#SECTION_PERFORMANCE](https://slurm.schedmd.com/sbatch.html)
Executing sbatch sends a remote procedure call to slurmctld . If
enough calls from sbatch or other Slurm client commands that send remote
procedure calls to the slurmctld daemon come in at once, it can result in
a degradation of performance of the slurmctld daemon, possibly resulting
in a denial of service.
Do not run sbatch or other Slurm client commands that send remote
procedure calls to slurmctld from loops in shell scripts or other
programs. Ensure that programs limit calls to sbatch to the minimum
necessary for the information you are trying to gather.

A job which is to be dependent upon an entire job array should specify
itself dependent upon the ArrayJobID.
Since each array element can have a different exit code, the interpretation of
the afterok and afternotok clauses will be based upon the highest
exit code from any task in the job array.
When a job dependency specifies the job ID of a job array:
The after clause is satisfied after all tasks in the job array start.
The afterany clause is satisfied after all tasks in the job array
complete.

specified job has completed successfully (ran to completion with an exit code of

Snippet:
## EXAMPLES[#SECTION_EXAMPLES](https://slurm.schedmd.com/sbatch.html)
Specify a batch script by filename on the command line. The batch script specifies a 1 minute time limit for the job.
```text
$ cat myscript #!/bin/sh #SBATCH --time=1 srun hostname |sort $ sbatch -N4 myscript salloc: Granted job allocation 65537 $ cat slurm-65537.out host1 host2 host3 host4
```
Pass a batch script to sbatch on standard input:
```text
$ sbatch -N4 #!/bin/sh > srun hostname |sort > EOF sbatch: Submitted batch job 65541 $ cat slurm-65541.out host1 host2 host3 host4
```
To create a heterogeneous job with 3 components, each allocating a unique set of nodes:
```text
$ sbatch -w node[2-3] : -w node4 : -w node[5-7] work.bash Submitted batch job 34987
```

## Burst Buffers [#burst_buffer](https://slurm.schedmd.com/heterogeneous_jobs.html)
A burst buffer can either be persistent or linked to a specific job ID.
Since a heterogeneous job consists of multiple job IDs, a job-specific burst
buffer will be associated with only one heterogeneous job component.
Each component can have its own burst buffer directives, and they are processed
separately. Only a persistent burst buffer can be accessed by all components
of a heterogeneous job. Persistent burst buffers are only available in the
datawarp plugin. A sample batch script demonstrating this for the datawarp

## Job Dependencies [#dependencies](https://slurm.schedmd.com/burst_buffer.html)
If two jobs use burst buffers and one is dependent on the other (e.g.
`sbatch --dependency=afterok:123 ...`) then the second job will not
begin until the first job completes and its burst buffer stage-out completes.
If the second job does not use a burst buffer, but is dependent upon the first
job's completion, then it will not wait for the stage-out operation of the first
job to complete.
The second job can be made to wait for the first job's stage-out operation to
complete using the "afterburstbuffer" dependency option (e.g.
`sbatch --dependency=afterburstbuffer:123 ...`).

Executing sbatch sends a remote procedure call to slurmctld . If
enough calls from sbatch or other Slurm client commands that send remote
procedure calls to the slurmctld daemon come in at once, it can result in
a degradation of performance of the slurmctld daemon, possibly resulting
in a denial of service.

procedure calls to slurmctld from loops in shell scripts or other
programs. Ensure that programs limit calls to sbatch to the minimum
necessary for the information you are trying to gather.

## EXAMPLES[#SECTION_EXAMPLES](https://slurm.schedmd.com/sbatch.html)
Specify a batch script by filename on the command line. The batch script specifies a 1 minute time limit for the job.
```text
$ cat myscript #!/bin/sh #SBATCH --time=1 srun hostname |sort $ sbatch -N4 myscript salloc: Granted job allocation 65537 $ cat slurm-65537.out host1 host2 host3 host4
```
Pass a batch script to sbatch on standard input:
```text
$ sbatch -N4 #!/bin/sh > srun hostname |sort > EOF sbatch: Submitted batch job 65541 $ cat slurm-65541.out host1 host2 host3 host4
```
To create a heterogeneous job with 3 components, each allocating a unique set of nodes:
```text
$ sbatch -w node[2-3] : -w node4 : -w node[5-7] work.bash Submitted batch job 34987
```

## Burst Buffers [#burst_buffer](https://slurm.schedmd.com/heterogeneous_jobs.html)
A burst buffer can either be persistent or linked to a specific job ID.
Since a heterogeneous job consists of multiple job IDs, a job-specific burst
buffer will be associated with only one heterogeneous job component.
Each component can have its own burst buffer directives, and they are processed
separately. Only a persistent burst buffer can be accessed by all components
of a heterogeneous job. Persistent burst buffers are only available in the
datawarp plugin. A sample batch script demonstrating this for the datawarp
plugin is appended.

The srun command is used to launch applications.
By default, the application is launched only on the first component of a
heterogeneous job, but options are available to support different behaviors.
srun's "--het-group" option defines which hetjob component(s) are to have
applications launched for them. The --het-group option takes an expression
defining which component(s) are to launch an application for an individual
execution of the srun command. The expression can contain one or more component

in a hyphen separated list. By default, an application is launched only on

## Limitations [#limitations](https://slurm.schedmd.com/heterogeneous_jobs.html)
The backfill scheduler has limitations in how it tracks usage of CPUs and
memory in the future.
This typically requires the backfill scheduler be able to allocate each
component of a heterogeneous job on a different node in order to begin its
resource allocation, even if multiple components of the job do actually get
allocated resources on the same node.

be eligible to migrate between clusters or to have different components of
the job execute on different clusters in the federation.

## Job Dependencies [#dependencies](https://slurm.schedmd.com/job_array.html)
A job which is to be dependent upon an entire job array should specify
itself dependent upon the ArrayJobID.
Since each array element can have a different exit code, the interpretation of
the afterok and afternotok clauses will be based upon the highest
exit code from any task in the job array.
When a job dependency specifies the job ID of a job array:
The after clause is satisfied after all tasks in the job array start.
The afterany clause is satisfied after all tasks in the job array
complete.
The aftercorr clause is satisfied after the corresponding task ID in the
specified job has completed successfully (ran to completion with an exit code of
zero).
The afterok clause is satisfied after all tasks in the job array

The backfill scheduler has limitations in how it tracks usage of CPUs and
memory in the future.
This typically requires the backfill scheduler be able to allocate each
component of a heterogeneous job on a different node in order to begin its

allocated resources on the same node.

The srun command is always used for job step creation. It fills in

## PERFORMANCE[#SECTION_PERFORMANCE](https://slurm.schedmd.com/sbatch.html)
Executing sbatch sends a remote procedure call to slurmctld . If
enough calls from sbatch or other Slurm client commands that send remote
procedure calls to the slurmctld daemon come in at once, it can result in
a degradation of performance of the slurmctld daemon, possibly resulting
in a denial of service.
Do not run sbatch or other Slurm client commands that send remote
procedure calls to slurmctld from loops in shell scripts or other
programs. Ensure that programs limit calls to sbatch to the minimum
necessary for the information you are trying to gather.

## EXAMPLES[#SECTION_EXAMPLES](https://slurm.schedmd.com/sbatch.html)
Specify a batch script by filename on the command line. The batch script specifies a 1 minute time limit for the job.
```text
$ cat myscript #!/bin/sh #SBATCH --time=1 srun hostname |sort $ sbatch -N4 myscript salloc: Granted job allocation 65537 $ cat slurm-65537.out host1 host2 host3 host4
```
Pass a batch script to sbatch on standard input:
```text
$ sbatch -N4 #!/bin/sh > srun hostname |sort > EOF sbatch: Submitted batch job 65541 $ cat slurm-65541.out host1 host2 host3 host4
```
To create a heterogeneous job with 3 components, each allocating a unique set of nodes:
```text
$ sbatch -w node[2-3] : -w node4 : -w node[5-7] work.bash Submitted batch job 34987
```

## Job Dependencies [#dependencies](https://slurm.schedmd.com/burst_buffer.html)
If two jobs use burst buffers and one is dependent on the other (e.g.
`sbatch --dependency=afterok:123 ...`) then the second job will not
begin until the first job completes and its burst buffer stage-out completes.
If the second job does not use a burst buffer, but is dependent upon the first
job's completion, then it will not wait for the stage-out operation of the first
job to complete.
The second job can be made to wait for the first job's stage-out operation to
complete using the "afterburstbuffer" dependency option (e.g.
`sbatch --dependency=afterburstbuffer:123 ...`).

A job which is to be dependent upon an entire job array should specify
itself dependent upon the ArrayJobID.

the afterok and afternotok clauses will be based upon the highest

## PERFORMANCE[#SECTION_PERFORMANCE](https://slurm.schedmd.com/sbatch.html)
Executing sbatch sends a remote procedure call to slurmctld . If
enough calls from sbatch or other Slurm client commands that send remote
procedure calls to the slurmctld daemon come in at once, it can result in
a degradation of performance of the slurmctld daemon, possibly resulting
in a denial of service.
Do not run sbatch or other Slurm client commands that send remote
procedure calls to slurmctld from loops in shell scripts or other
programs. Ensure that programs limit calls to sbatch to the minimum
necessary for the information you are trying to gather.

## PERFORMANCE[#SECTION_PERFORMANCE](https://slurm.schedmd.com/sbatch.html)
Executing sbatch sends a remote procedure call to slurmctld . If
enough calls from sbatch or other Slurm client commands that send remote
procedure calls to the slurmctld daemon come in at once, it can result in
a degradation of performance of the slurmctld daemon, possibly resulting
in a denial of service.
Do not run sbatch or other Slurm client commands that send remote
procedure calls to slurmctld from loops in shell scripts or other
programs. Ensure that programs limit calls to sbatch to the minimum
necessary for the information you are trying to gather.

Snippet:
## PERFORMANCE[#SECTION_PERFORMANCE](https://slurm.schedmd.com/sbatch.html)
Executing sbatch sends a remote procedure call to slurmctld . If
enough calls from sbatch or other Slurm client commands that send remote
procedure calls to the slurmctld daemon come in at once, it can result in
a degradation of performance of the slurmctld daemon, possibly resulting
in a denial of service.
Do not run sbatch or other Slurm client commands that send remote
procedure calls to slurmctld from loops in shell scripts or other
programs. Ensure that programs limit calls to sbatch to the minimum
necessary for the information you are trying to gather.

## EXAMPLES[#SECTION_EXAMPLES](https://slurm.schedmd.com/sbatch.html)
Specify a batch script by filename on the command line. The batch script specifies a 1 minute time limit for the job.
```text
$ cat myscript #!/bin/sh #SBATCH --time=1 srun hostname |sort $ sbatch -N4 myscript salloc: Granted job allocation 65537 $ cat slurm-65537.out host1 host2 host3 host4
```
Pass a batch script to sbatch on standard input:
```text
$ sbatch -N4 #!/bin/sh > srun hostname |sort > EOF sbatch: Submitted batch job 65541 $ cat slurm-65541.out host1 host2 host3 host4
```
To create a heterogeneous job with 3 components, each allocating a unique set of nodes:
```text
$ sbatch -w node[2-3] : -w node4 : -w node[5-7] work.bash Submitted batch job 34987
```

## Burst Buffers [#burst_buffer](https://slurm.schedmd.com/heterogeneous_jobs.html)
A burst buffer can either be persistent or linked to a specific job ID.
Since a heterogeneous job consists of multiple job IDs, a job-specific burst
buffer will be associated with only one heterogeneous job component.
Each component can have its own burst buffer directives, and they are processed
separately. Only a persistent burst buffer can be accessed by all components
of a heterogeneous job. Persistent burst buffers are only available in the
datawarp plugin. A sample batch script demonstrating this for the datawarp
plugin is appended.

## Job Dependencies [#dependencies](https://slurm.schedmd.com/burst_buffer.html)
If two jobs use burst buffers and one is dependent on the other (e.g.
`sbatch --dependency=afterok:123 ...`) then the second job will not
begin until the first job completes and its burst buffer stage-out completes.
If the second job does not use a burst buffer, but is dependent upon the first
job's completion, then it will not wait for the stage-out operation of the first
job to complete.
The second job can be made to wait for the first job's stage-out operation to
complete using the "afterburstbuffer" dependency option (e.g.
`sbatch --dependency=afterburstbuffer:123 ...`).

## PERFORMANCE[#SECTION_PERFORMANCE](https://slurm.schedmd.com/sbatch.html)
Executing sbatch sends a remote procedure call to slurmctld . If
enough calls from sbatch or other Slurm client commands that send remote
procedure calls to the slurmctld daemon come in at once, it can result in
a degradation of performance of the slurmctld daemon, possibly resulting
in a denial of service.
Do not run sbatch or other Slurm client commands that send remote
procedure calls to slurmctld from loops in shell scripts or other
programs. Ensure that programs limit calls to sbatch to the minimum
necessary for the information you are trying to gather.

Since a heterogeneous job consists of multiple job IDs, a job-specific burst
buffer will be associated with only one heterogeneous job component.
Each component can have its own burst buffer directives, and they are processed
separately. Only a persistent burst buffer can be accessed by all components
of a heterogeneous job. Persistent burst buffers are only available in the
datawarp plugin. A sample batch script demonstrating this for the datawarp
plugin is appended.

## PERFORMANCE[#SECTION_PERFORMANCE](https://slurm.schedmd.com/sbatch.html)
Executing sbatch sends a remote procedure call to slurmctld . If
enough calls from sbatch or other Slurm client commands that send remote
procedure calls to the slurmctld daemon come in at once, it can result in
a degradation of performance of the slurmctld daemon, possibly resulting
in a denial of service.
Do not run sbatch or other Slurm client commands that send remote
procedure calls to slurmctld from loops in shell scripts or other
programs. Ensure that programs limit calls to sbatch to the minimum
necessary for the information you are trying to gather.

## PERFORMANCE[#SECTION_PERFORMANCE](https://slurm.schedmd.com/sbatch.html)
Executing sbatch sends a remote procedure call to slurmctld . If
enough calls from sbatch or other Slurm client commands that send remote
procedure calls to the slurmctld daemon come in at once, it can result in
a degradation of performance of the slurmctld daemon, possibly resulting
in a denial of service.
Do not run sbatch or other Slurm client commands that send remote
procedure calls to slurmctld from loops in shell scripts or other
programs. Ensure that programs limit calls to sbatch to the minimum
necessary for the information you are trying to gather.

## Job Dependencies [#dependencies](https://slurm.schedmd.com/burst_buffer.html)
If two jobs use burst buffers and one is dependent on the other (e.g.
`sbatch --dependency=afterok:123 ...`) then the second job will not
begin until the first job completes and its burst buffer stage-out completes.
If the second job does not use a burst buffer, but is dependent upon the first
job's completion, then it will not wait for the stage-out operation of the first
job to complete.
The second job can be made to wait for the first job's stage-out operation to
complete using the "afterburstbuffer" dependency option (e.g.
`sbatch --dependency=afterburstbuffer:123 ...`).

itself dependent upon the ArrayJobID.

## PERFORMANCE[#SECTION_PERFORMANCE](https://slurm.schedmd.com/sbatch.html)
Executing sbatch sends a remote procedure call to slurmctld . If
enough calls from sbatch or other Slurm client commands that send remote
procedure calls to the slurmctld daemon come in at once, it can result in
a degradation of performance of the slurmctld daemon, possibly resulting
in a denial of service.
Do not run sbatch or other Slurm client commands that send remote
procedure calls to slurmctld from loops in shell scripts or other
programs. Ensure that programs limit calls to sbatch to the minimum
necessary for the information you are trying to gather.

## EXAMPLES[#SECTION_EXAMPLES](https://slurm.schedmd.com/sbatch.html)
Specify a batch script by filename on the command line. The batch script specifies a 1 minute time limit for the job.
```text
$ cat myscript #!/bin/sh #SBATCH --time=1 srun hostname |sort $ sbatch -N4 myscript salloc: Granted job allocation 65537 $ cat slurm-65537.out host1 host2 host3 host4
```
Pass a batch script to sbatch on standard input:
```text
$ sbatch -N4 #!/bin/sh > srun hostname |sort > EOF sbatch: Submitted batch job 65541 $ cat slurm-65541.out host1 host2 host3 host4
```
To create a heterogeneous job with 3 components, each allocating a unique set of nodes:
```text
$ sbatch -w node[2-3] : -w node4 : -w node[5-7] work.bash Submitted batch job 34987
```

## PERFORMANCE[#SECTION_PERFORMANCE](https://slurm.schedmd.com/sbatch.html)
Executing sbatch sends a remote procedure call to slurmctld . If
enough calls from sbatch or other Slurm client commands that send remote
procedure calls to the slurmctld daemon come in at once, it can result in
a degradation of performance of the slurmctld daemon, possibly resulting
in a denial of service.
Do not run sbatch or other Slurm client commands that send remote
procedure calls to slurmctld from loops in shell scripts or other
programs. Ensure that programs limit calls to sbatch to the minimum
necessary for the information you are trying to gather.

The backfill scheduler has limitations in how it tracks usage of CPUs and
memory in the future.

results.prompt: Use official Slurm docs to explain QOS limits such as MaxJobs and MaxCPUs
results.agent_response:
Here’s a concise, doc‑based explanation of common QOS limits (with behavior notes and examples). Sources: Slurm QOS and Resource Limits pages (https://slurm.schedmd.com/qos.html, https://slurm.schedmd.com/resource_limits.html).

What a QOS limit is
- A QOS limit caps a resource or submission metric for jobs that request that QOS. QOS limits mirror limits that can also be set on user/account/partition/cluster associations; when a QOS defines a limit it overrides association limits (see precedence below).

Key limits (definitions)
- MaxJobs
  - Maximum number of jobs that may be concurrently active (RUNNING or PENDING as enforced) that are associated with that QOS (or that count point in the hierarchy).
  - If a submission would cause the limit to be exceeded the job will pend unless the QOS has Flags=DenyOnLimit (see DenyOnLimit).
- MaxCPUs
  - Maximum number of CPUs (cores) that may be concurrently allocated to jobs using that QOS. This is enforced against the sum of CPU allocations for matching jobs.
  - CPUs are counted as integer core units (not time-weighted).
- MaxNodes / MinNodes / Max[Time|Wall]
  - Limits on node counts or job wall time. (Note: some of these limits have special precedence rules; see hierarchy note.)
- MaxSubmitJobs, MaxSubmitJobsPerUser
  - Limits on the number of jobs that may be submitted within some context (global, per-user, etc.). These control submission rate/quantity rather than resource allocation.
- MaxTRES / GrpTRES / MaxTRESPerNode
  - TRES = Trackable RESources (e.g., cpu, mem, gres/gpu). MaxTRES can set absolute limits on TRES usage (for example cpu=2000,gpu=10,mem=100000).
  - GrpTRES limits group (aggregate) usage across the QOS.
  - MaxTRESPerNode or Max[Something]PerNode is applied per node.
- MaxGRES / GRES-related limits
  - Limits specifically for GRES (Generic RESources) such as GPUs; used when you want to constrain GPU counts.
- Flags=Relative
  - When set, numeric limits are treated as percentages of total cluster resources (e.g., cpu=50 means 50% of all CPUs). Memory limits should be set without units when using Relative (1MB = 1%).

Behavioral rules and enforcement
- Hierarchy / precedence
  - Limits are enforced according to a fixed hierarchy (partition QOS, job QOS, user association, account association(s) ascending, root/cluster association, partition limit, none). The first place a limit is defined in this list is used. You can change partition-vs-job QOS precedence with Flags=OverPartQOS.
- What happens when a limit would be exceeded
  - Default: a job that would violate a Max* limit will pend until resources are available.
  - If Flags=DenyOnLimit is set on the QOS, jobs that would violate the QOS “Max” limits will be denied at submission time (rejected), rather than pended.
  - Group (Grp) limits are treated as Max limits when DenyOnLimit is applied.
- Interaction with partitions and associations
  - A Partition QOS (a QOS attached to a partition) carries the QOS limits into the partition view and (by default) is applied before a job’s requested QOS. OverPartQOS reverses that order.
- Relative QOS nuance
  - With Flags=Relative, limits are percentages and may be computed either cluster-wide or relative to a partition when used as a partition QOS; slurmctld must be reconfigured/restarted to pick up some flag changes.
- Units and types
  - CPU limits are counts. Memory limits are normally specified with units (MB/GB) but when using Relative you should set memory with no units so it’s treated as a percentage.

Examples (from docs)
- If a partition QOS sets MaxJobs=20 and a user-association sets MaxJobs=4, the partition QOS value (20) takes effect because of the hierarchy—unless OverPartQOS is used to reverse precedence.
- If a QOS has cpu=50 and Flags=Relative, that means jobs using the QOS can consume up to 50% of total cluster CPUs (values above 100 are treated as 100).

Practical notes for admins and users
- Use MaxTRES (or specific MaxCPUs/MaxGRES) when you need precise control over specific resource types (CPUs vs GPUs vs memory).
- Use DenyOnLimit when you prefer immediate rejection at submission instead of a job silently queueing/pend-ing.
- Remember the hierarchy: setting limits at the right level (partition vs QOS vs association) matters.
- When changing QOS flags or limits, reconfiguration may be required for some flags (e.g., Relative) to take effect.

Where to read more
- QOS reference and options: https://slurm.schedmd.com/qos.html
- Resource limits and hierarchy: https://slurm.schedmd.com/resource_limits.html

If you want, I can:
- extract the exact sacctmgr commands to set common limits (e.g., set MaxCPUs for QOS foo) and give examples, or
- show how a submission would be evaluated under a specific set of QOS/partition/association limits you provide. Which would you like?

A QOS can be attached to a partition. This means the partition will have all

## Initial Testing [#INITIAL_TESTING](https://slurm.schedmd.com/nss_slurm.html)
Before enabling NSS Slurm directly on the node, you should use the
-s slurm option to getent within a newly launched job step
to verify that the rest of the setup has been completed successfully. The
-s option to getent allows it to query a specific database —
even if it has not been enabled by default through the system's
nsswitch.conf . Note that nss_slurm only responds to requests from
processes within the job step itself — you must launch the getent
command within a job step to see any data returned.

tim@blackhole:~$ srun getent -s slurm passwd tim:x:1000:1000:Tim Wickberg:/home/tim:/bin/bash tim@blackhole:~$ srun getent -s slurm group tim:x:1000:tim projecta:x:1001:tim

calculation, the "PriorityWeightQOS" configuration parameter must be
defined in the slurm.conf file and assigned an integer value greater
